intro: College history teachers research, explain and manage a heavy teaching load, skills used in social science research and education leadership. The closest of the 25 careers below is Sociologists, with an 80% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $106,030, which is 26% more than the $83,820 history teachers in higher education earn.
why_it_works: Teaching history at college level means turning research into clear lectures, grading arguments fairly and keeping a course on schedule. O*NET rates instructing at 4 out of 5 for this job, time management at 3.75 and judgment at 3.62. Social science research, curriculum work and archives use the same skills. Every match needs no more education than you already have. The gaps are technology and coordination.
tips: Political Scientists earn $142,080, which is 70% more, and are a 77% match.
Instructional Coordinators are a 76% match if you want to design courses rather than teach them.
Postsecondary education administrators earn $104,590, or 25% more, and value teaching experience.

faq.q: What jobs can former history professors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Sociologists (80%), secondary school teachers (77%) and Political Scientists (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Historians are 75% matched and earn $76,750, which is 8% less than the $83,820 median for postsecondary history teachers, but focus fully on research.

faq.q: Which careers for history professors pay more?
faq.a: 8 of the 25 matches pay more. Political Scientists earn $142,080 (70% more), Sociologists $106,030 (26% more) and postsecondary education administrators $104,590 (25% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three use your research and writing skills.

faq.q: Do history professors need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than history teachers in higher education already have, including all of the top 10. A doctoral degree is common in the closest match, held by 50% of workers, so your graduate training covers most requirements.

faq.q: What skills should history professors learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are technology design, social perceptiveness, coordination and quality control analysis. Complex problem solving already rates 3.38 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so data and management skills are the main steps outside teaching.
